classification.difficultyReason: Match sine-difference coefficients, including surds and an exact inverse-tangent angle.

content.prompt: Express the following in the form $R\sin(x-\alpha)$.

answer.worked:
Expand the sine difference and equate coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}8\sin x-6\cos x&=R(\sin x\cos\alpha-\cos x\sin\alpha)\\R\cos\alpha&=8\\R\sin\alpha&=6\\R&=\sqrt{8^2+6^2}=10\\\tan\alpha&=\frac68=\frac34\end{align*}$$
Both $\cos\alpha$ and $\sin\alpha$ are positive, so choose $\alpha$ in the first quadrant.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac34\right)\\8\sin x-6\cos x&=10\sin\left(x-\tan^{-1}\left(\frac34\right)\right)\end{align*}$$

Expand the sine difference and equate coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}2\sqrt2\sin x-\cos x&=R(\sin x\cos\alpha-\cos x\sin\alpha)\\R\cos\alpha&=2\sqrt2\\R\sin\alpha&=1\\R&=\sqrt{(2\sqrt2)^2+1^2}=3\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}\end{align*}$$
Both $\cos\alpha$ and $\sin\alpha$ are positive, so choose $\alpha$ in the first quadrant.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}\right)\\2\sqrt2\sin x-\cos x&=3\sin\left(x-\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}\right)\right)\end{align*}$$

Expand the sine difference and equate coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}\sqrt3\sin x-3\cos x&=R(\sin x\cos\alpha-\cos x\sin\alpha)\\R\cos\alpha&=\sqrt3\\R\sin\alpha&=3\\R&=\sqrt{(\sqrt3)^2+3^2}=2\sqrt3\\\tan\alpha&=\frac3{\sqrt3}=\sqrt3\end{align*}$$
Both $\cos\alpha$ and $\sin\alpha$ are positive, so choose $\alpha$ in the first quadrant.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\frac\pi3\\\sqrt3\sin x-3\cos x&=2\sqrt3\sin\left(x-\frac\pi3\right)\end{align*}$$
